rounds.text: Vardhman Acrylics trades at an attractive P/E of 8.91x and a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.46x, offering a healthy 3.24% dividend yield [E1, E2, E4]. The company operates completely debt-free with borrowings at zero, while maintaining strong efficiency metrics such as an ROA of 12.18% and an ROCE of 11.42% that outperform sector benchmarks [E8, E10, E38]. Recent fundamental performance shows dramatic operational acceleration, highlighted by a 352% surge in trailing twelve-month profit growth and an operating margin expanding to 23% in June 2026 compared to -1% a year prior [E21, E31]. Valuation models underscore this mispricing, as a discounted cash flow intrinsic value sits at Rs 58 per share—providing a 20.0% margin of safety—and a reverse DCF indicates the current price pessimistically implies negative earnings growth [E44, E45, E46]. Furthermore, strong technical positioning is confirmed by a relative-strength rating of 95 against the Nifty 500 alongside prices sitting above both 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E49, E50]. Conceded: compounded sales and profit growth over longer 3, 5, and 10-year horizons have been negative or low, reflecting historical top-line stagnation [E14, E15, E16, E18, E19, E20].

Vardhman Acrylics Ltd suffers from an acute, long-term secular growth stagnation, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of -3% over 10 years and -9% over 3 years [E14, E16]. This top-line erosion directly feeds into an equally dismal profit profile, featuring a 10-year compounded profit growth of -4% and a 5-year contraction of -9% [E18, E19]. Compounding these fundamental issues, working capital efficiency has degraded severely, with working capital days surging from 81.0 days to 219 days [E65]. Furthermore, earnings quality is highly suspect because the reported numbers rely on a low tax rate and include Rs 15.5 Cr of other income [E62, E64].
